layers.process: Entry permit for non-East African visitors: US$70.80 per adult and US$23.60 per child (about A$100.57 and A$33.52 at RBA, 30 October 2026: A$1 = US$0.7040); under 5 free. Foreign-registered vehicle permit from US$47.20 (up to 2,000 kg) to US$354 (7,001 kg and above); crater service fee US$295 per vehicle trip (about A$419). A permit is valid for one entry within 24 hours. NCAA says tariffs may change without notice.
A licensed guide or an official NCAA guide must accompany all crater visitors. Authorised walking safaris must be accompanied by an armed NCAA ranger.

Off-road driving is not permitted unless the Conservation Commissioner authorises it. Speed limits are 50 km/h in the area and 25 km/h at the craters. Only 4x4 vehicles up to 3,500 kg tare weight may enter the crater floor. NCAA's page gives two different crater gate closing times (16:00 and 18:00): confirm with NCAA.

laws.rule: Photographing local people is prohibited except in designated Cultural Bomas. Commercial filming needs a filming permit. Keep at least 25 metres from animals.
NCAA asks visitors not to use profanity or engage in dangerous, illegal or offensive behaviour, and not to harass, feed or throw objects at wild animals.
